newsitem.title: UK: Merrill strategists keep lead in Reuter poll.
newsitem.headline: Merrill strategists keep lead in Reuter poll.

text.p: Strategists at Merrill Lynch maintained their position as top-rated group among fund managers for pan-European equity research, according to a poll published by Reuters on Tuesday.

The Merrill European strategy team of David Bowers, Brian Allworthy and Plum Shipton was rated top by of 22.4 percent of the 100 investment groups questioned, weighted to reflect the size of continental European funds they had under management. The Merrill vote dropped from 27.4 percent last year, allowing strategists at second-placed Morgan Stanley to cut the lead held by their rival U.S.-owned house.
Allworthy said Merrill's links with specialists outside the brokerage was a particularly significant part of its service.

"What really paid off for us is access we can give to the intellectual property rights of the group in terms of industry and academic research, allowing fund managers to directly access specialists in finance and economics," he said.

Fund manager polls such as the annual Reuters continental European survey, carried out by Tempest Consultants, are significant for analysts in London's broking industry both as an indicator of how fund managers perceive their service and because top-rated analysts can command premium salaries.
The Morgan Stanley team led by Richard Davidson saw its vote rise to 19.8 percent from 14.6 percent last year.
UBS European strategists maintained their third position, although their vote slipped from 12.7 percent from 11.2 percent.
At Merrill, Allworthy welcomed his group's continuing high rating but said he hoped the narrowing of the lead reflected healthy competition between brokerages and strategists.

"I was pleased to see our position but I note the lead we had last year has been much reduced," Allworthy said. "And I would like to think that's because there's more healthy competition in the sector."
